case_schema.description: The structure of one case per section. A rule case runs rule_documents[document] on its input ({text}, or {value, before, after}: the element inserted into the text); outputs compare with their JSON type.

identity: The rule-set identity (D38-4) is the lower-case hex SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) bytes of the rule-set document AS RECEIVED: the parsed JSON values, before any default is applied, never a re-serialisation of a model. JCS: object keys sorted by UTF-16 code units; no whitespace; numbers are values written in ECMAScript Number-to-string form (1 and 1.0 are the same number and hash the same; 1e21 is 1e+21; -0 is 0); strings UTF-8 with only the quote, the backslash and U+0000-U+001F escaped. ABSENT AND EMPTY DIFFER: an omitted list (vetoes, renderings, decoys, substitutions) and an empty list are different documents with different digests, so a consumer hashes what it received and never adds or drops an empty list. An integer outside +/-(2^53 - 1) is refused (unsafe_integer). Every rule_set_identity case is reproducible from this file alone: parse 'document', apply JCS, compare with 'canonical_utf8' (the exact bytes, as a JSON string) and 'sha256'.
precedence: The vector is the truth (FR-016.9): a case with an external source outranks every implementation, miDataworks' included. A gap is closed by adding a case here first; the case is red in whichever app is wrong until it is fixed, then consumers re-vendor. Cases are append-only per validator version (a changed verdict is a new version).
renderings: What each rendering builtin does (D38-3; the same words as the schema $comment). render: spaced = the value's characters joined by one space; split_lines = joined by one newline (U+000A); spelled_out_digits = each ASCII digit as its lower-case English word (zero ... nine), every other character kept, the tokens joined by one space; mapping = left to right, the longest key matching at a position replaced by its value, a character no key matches kept. normaliser: digits_only = keep ASCII digits; strip_delimiters = remove U+0020, U+000A, '-' and '.'; words_to_digits = the inverse of spelled_out_digits (tokens separated by exactly one space; a digit word becomes its digit, any other token is one kept character); mapping_inverse = the mapping inverted (distinct values), applied the same way.

rule_set_identity.note: RFC 8785: keys sorted at every level, separators , and :, no whitespace
non-ASCII characters are written as UTF-8, never \u escapes
absent and empty differ: an empty vetoes list is part of the document, so a different hash from identity.minimal, which omits vetoes
numbers are values in ECMAScript form: 1.5 is 1.5, 1 is 1, -1 is -1
1.0 and 1 are the same number: RFC 8785 writes 1, so the SAME bytes and hash as identity.integer_weight
2^53 - 1 = 9007199254740991 is written exactly; a parser that reads JSON numbers as doubles keeps it; one more is refused (refuse.document.unsafe_integer)
keys sort by UTF-16 code units, not code points: U+1F600 (surrogates D83D DE00) sorts BEFORE U+FB01; a code-point sort puts it after

validator_scans: How the two IBAN validator versions find candidates in a text (every other validator's scan is pinned by its cases). iban@1: every non-overlapping match, left to right, of the regular expression [A-Za-z]{2}[0-9]{2}(?: ?[A-Za-z0-9])+ (so a spaced IBAN followed by a word runs on through the word; case iban.scan.absorbs_following_word). iban@2 (D38-1): search left to right for a head [A-Za-z]{2}[0-9]{2}, resuming at the end of the previous candidate; the candidate is the whole ASCII letter-and-digit run the head starts. Then, while the next character is one space followed by a letter-and-digit group, the group joins the candidate only when (1) the head's first two letters, read in either case, name a country of the SWIFT IBAN Registry; (2) the compact length (letters and digits) stays within that country's registered IBAN length; and (3) each character of the group fits the country's BBAN at its position (n a digit, a a letter, c a letter or digit; letters in either case). An unlisted country takes no group. Each candidate's value is checked by iban@1's check, unchanged.
